comment: Checks this plugin can run against a USER'S repo, for project_gates.py to discover.
A plugin declares its own; the runner never hardcodes a list, so adding a check here is the
whole registration step and a new plugin needs no change to the runner.
applies_when: every path must exist in the user's repo, or the check reports NOT APPLICABLE.
Both checks here decide applicability themselves (exit 3), because a Next.js project's routes
live in app/ OR src/app/ and its linting may not be installed: one path in applies_when cannot say so.
requires: executables that must be on PATH. Missing is a FAILURE, not a skip.

checks.why: The React frontend architecture's anti-patterns that a REAL run of eslint-config-next misses (measured, docs/evidence/audits/2026-10-21-react-frontend-claims.md): a client route file with no declared reason (R8), fetch inside a useEffect in a client module (R16), and an internal <a href="/..."> (R6; @next/next/no-html-link-for-pages only reads a pages/ directory). A gate: any finding fails; a client route that is a deliberate trade-off passes by declaring it with a reason. Not applicable outside the App Router.
Proves check_react_patterns.py still tells each pattern from its near miss in THIS project's Python.

Three official eslint-plugin-react rules that eslint-config-next ships OFF, each measured to catch an anti-pattern the React skill names: react/no-array-index-key (R4), react/jsx-no-constructed-context-values (R15, including React 19's <Ctx value> form), react/no-danger (R21). Run alone, through the project's own ESLint, so the project's lint step keeps every other rule. Not applicable where eslint-config-next is not installed.
Proves check_react_lint.py turns exactly those three rules on, keeps every other rule off, and reports a project without ESLint as not applicable.
